_comment: Accepted findings for check-editor-render-parity.js (CHECK A: editor-canvas desync — a destructured+written attribute never referenced in the preview JSX; CHECK B: invalid CSS keyword passthrough — a SelectControl option value not in the target CSS property's valid keyword set). Same discipline as dead-controls-baseline.json: the guard reports NET-NEW findings only (findings NOT listed here). To accept a finding, add it here with a reason; to fix one, wire the attribute into the preview / correct the SelectControl option, then delete the entry. Empty `accepted` = zero tolerance once/if this is promoted to gate — it ships advisory-only today (2026-08-13), so nothing needs baselining yet; findings are census output, not a blocking backlog. CRITICAL: never raise the baseline silently — any increase must include a written reason (see check-element-manifest-conformance.js:796-798).

_meta.dispositionVocabularyNote: Closed vocabulary: by-design (correct, will never need fixing) / accepted-debt (real gap, consciously deferred) / detector-limitation (the checker itself is wrong — flags a rule violation per THE-MIGRATION-METHOD.md:455, not a normal outcome) / blocked (waiting on something external). See .claude/parking.md P-BASELINE-DISPOSITION-VOCABULARY / .claude/LEDGER.md.

Verified by hand: field_id() builds the id/for pair (non-paint, id/for/name are already-exempt native functional attrs); field_label() echoes the visible <label> text, but that text comes from the block's OWN 'label' attribute, not fieldName. No visible editor-canvas effect is missing.

Cross-file consumption blind spot (2026-08-13 refinement 2): transitionDuration's only render.php appearance is as part of the whole $attributes array passed to sgs_transition_vars() in includes/helpers-tokens.php, which the detector's dataflow trace can't follow across files. Verified by hand: it emits --sgs-transition-duration, a motion-timing custom property consumed only by a :hover/transition rule — the same non-paint category signal 1 already exempts when the consumption is in-file.
Same shape as sgs/post-grid transitionDuration — sgs_transition_vars() cross-file consumption, motion-timing non-paint custom property.

Feeds a live AnalyserNode <canvas> draw loop (Tier G, view.js reactive playerStyle rendering) — genuinely un-fixable the simple way, since there is no audio playback (hence no analyser data) in the static editor canvas to draw against. Bean-accepted 2026-08-13: leave as-is unless a real idea surfaces.

Vanilla IntersectionObserver/rAF scroll-linked opacity fade (view.js) — mutates a custom property only while the page is actively scrolling. No single static frame represents 'fades as you scroll past'; the editor canvas is non-scrollable.
Same shape as fadeOnScroll — a scroll-intersection-triggered SVG stroke-draw animation (vanilla IntersectionObserver, Tier V) with no static resting frame to preview.

Only rendered via a data-wp-text binding gated hidden until a real POST submission flips context.submitted (Interactivity API state) — cannot be simulated in the static editor without a real form submission.
Same shape as successMessage — consumed only by view.js's post-submit redirect logic, never rendered as visible content.
An anti-spam field deliberately rendered aria-hidden and visually invisible even on the real frontend for real visitors — invisible-by-design, not a preview gap.

Sprintf()-positional-argument blind spot: render.php builds the native file-input markup via sprintf('<input ... accept="%s"%s />', ..., $accept, ...) — the attribute name lives in the format string, the value is a later positional argument, a shape precedingHtmlAttributeName()'s adjacency-based scan can't trace. Verified by hand: $accept only ever reaches the native accept file-picker filter attribute (zero rendered paint, browser-native dialog only).

Selects between two semantically-equivalent HTML TAG NAMES (nav vs div) for the wrapper element — a genuinely non-visual a11y-landmark choice with no CSS/paint difference, a shape none of the four exemption signals cover (they classify attribute VALUES landing in a sink, not a tag-name choice). Verified by hand against render.php.

Cross-file consumption blind spot: thumbnailAlt's only render.php appearance is as a positional argument to the shared sgs_render_media() helper (includes/render-helpers.php), which resolves it internally to the alt attribute — a non-paint accessibility text value the single-file dataflow trace can't see land there.

GSAP ScrollTrigger scroll-scrub configuration (Tier G, data-sgs-fx-start on the canvas) — the block's own edit.js explicitly shows a static thumbnail with a Notice: 'Scroll effects preview on the live site. The editor always shows the thumbnail frame.' No static frame can represent a scroll-scrubbed frame sequence.
Same shape as fxStart — GSAP ScrollTrigger scroll-scrub config, no static resting frame; the block's own Notice already documents this.
Same shape as fxStart — GSAP ScrollTrigger scroll-scrub config, no static resting frame; the block's own Notice already documents this.
Same shape as fxStart — GSAP ScrollTrigger pin-during-scrub config, no static resting frame; the block's own Notice already documents this.

sgs/site-header's edit.js is a fully hand-authored InnerBlocks canvas with no ServerSideRender and no scoped-CSS mirror of render.php's <style> block — render.php's real scroll-timeline CSS (animation-timeline:scroll) never loads into the editor at all, for ANY of this block's scroll behaviours. A representative static preview isn't meaningful for a genuinely motion-over-scroll-time effect. Candidate for a future 5th structural signal (no-ServerSideRender + no scoped-CSS mirror), not built this pass — see LEDGER.
Same shape as headerShrink — no CSS from this block reaches the editor for any scroll behaviour, and hide-on-scroll-down has no meaningful static resting frame either way.

Sprintf()-positional-argument blind spot: render.php builds aria-label="%s" via sprintf() with $blockLabel as a later positional argument — the same shape as sgs/form-field-file's allowedTypes. Verified by hand: only ever reaches a native aria-label attribute, zero visual paint by definition.

edit.js already hardcodes the fully-revealed 'is-revealed' resting state on every canvas entry (the correct static representation regardless of the toggle) — the toggle itself only controls a one-shot IntersectionObserver stagger sequence that has no other static frame to show.
Same shape as revealOnScroll — a per-entry stagger delay for a scroll-triggered reveal sequence, no static frame beyond the already-correct fully-revealed canvas state.
Gates a JS-driven marquee animation (view.js) with no CSS of its own absent the animation — motion-over-time, no single static frame differs from the toggle being off.

URL-encoded into the wa.me link's query string only (render.php) — never rendered as visible text on the editor canvas OR the real frontend (the WhatsApp recipient sees it as a pre-filled chat message after clicking, not as page content). Non-visual by the nature of the mechanism, not a bug.

Drives only the OPEN-transition animation direction (render.php:399-435 -- an entry-animation CSS class hooked to @keyframes, resolved per-anchor when 'auto'). No static resting appearance differs between values; motion-over-time with no single frame to preview, same category as sgs/trust-bar's autoScroll and sgs/timeline's revealOnScroll/revealStagger.

2026-09-05 architecture-correction revert (D622/CLAUDE.md Colour controls section): 3548f7c85 wrongly moved the icon colour row out of the shared root SgsColourPanel into a bespoke ToolsPanelItem+DesignTokenPicker mount; that mount's onDeselect happened to reset iconColour+iconColourGradient+iconColourHover+iconColourHoverGradient in ONE setAttributes() call, which incidentally satisfied SIGNAL 2's companion-exemption (iconColour is read outside controls, via the iconPlaceholder preview's `color: iconColour`). Reverting to the correct SgsColourPanel row shape (each state's onChange/onGradientChange is its own single-key setAttributes() call, matching every other block's row shape) removes that incidental grouping and resurfaces this finding. The underlying gap is real and PRE-EXISTING, identical in the pre-3548f7c85 code (verified byte-for-byte against `git show 3548f7c85~1`): iconPlaceholder's editor preview only ever reflected the solid iconColour, never iconColourGradient, both before and after today's churn. It was never audited before because check-editor-render-parity's 0/128 close-out (358584e79 etc.) ran later the same day, against the wrong-shape code, so this exact shape was never exercised. Not introduced by this revert.
